newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA PARLIAMENT APPROVES TROOPS TO ALBANIA.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA PARLIAMENT APPROVES TROOPS TO ALBANIA.

text.p: Romania's parliament on Thursday overwhelmingly backed the dispatch of 400 troops to take part in an international peacekeeping force in lawless Albania.

A joint session of parliament's two chambers voted 231 to 61 with 64 abstentions to send the troops at the request of President Emil Constantinescu. The leftist and nationalist opposition voted against or abstained.

The Romanian contingent of the Italian-led force, made up of 392 infantry men and eight officers, is to be deployed starting next week in the Adriatic ports of Vlore and Sarande and the town of Gjirokaster in rebel-held southern Albania.
Opposition members objected to the costs of the operation, estimated at the equivalent of $9.5 million, saying the money would be better spent on humanitarian aid.

Parliament also approved Constantinescu's request to use the airport in the western Romanian city of Timisoara, on the border with Serbia and Hungary, as a logistics and supply base for the Albanian operation.

The operation is intended to secure Albania's main ports and airport and to give the Tirana government time to reorganise the armed forces ahead of elections planned for June. Romania's participation is generally viewed by the new centrist government as a means of promoting its longshot bid for early NATO membership. REUTER
